lines.english: I can't sleep.
The second hand of the clock has spun around countless times as I've been staring at it.
…Actually, I've been watching the minute hand spin around a few times too, but I still can't fall asleep.
Kazusa had already fallen asleep long ago.
She was still rather tense, but today, she chased me out of the bathroom and ate her food with her own hands.
Even after she slipped into bed, she glared at me for a while, and spoke to me at length about her additional concert and her plans for when she leaves Japan…
Tired from both speaking and her time outside, she defenselessly fell asleep right in front of me with soft breaths.
That's why I was finally able to relax today, and thought to myself that I'd be able to fall asleep easily…
But my memories are getting in the way.
Memories of the bombshell dropped on me this late in the game. The words that Youko-san spoke.
"…Excuse me?"
"Like I said, leukemia. Usually it's the unhappy heroine who falls ill with this disease, but it seems God has made a mistake yet again."
After forcefully tracking down Youko-san, who had concealed her own whereabouts, I came here to meet her in person toーof courseーtalk about Kazusa.
I wanted to tell her in earnest that I can no longer support Kazusa, and ask for her help…
And I wanted her to take the responsibility she had forced upon us up until now.
"It was about half a year ago, I think… My body felt unsteady from just playing a two-hour concert."
I wanted her to take responsibility. That way, Kazusa would have been saved… Yet…
"Around my third and fourth piece, my heartbeat went up and I couldn't breathe properly. Even when I was done with the concert it continued for about an hour."
Youko-san called me to a location I could never have imagined.
Houjou University Hospital…
"At first, I thought it was diabetes finally catching up to me."
"…Anyone would have thought that. You two should have more self-restraint."
"Haha, you never change, Guitar-kun. You act all high-and-mighty even to me."
"…I'm sorry. I haven't been able to take in the situation yet."
"…Well, I suppose so. It took me a decent while to accept it myself."
A fifteen minute walk from where I live…
Within the Houjou campus which I commuted to and from for around seven years, there is a hospital. In a private room of that hospital is where she lies.
"They told me I had anemia when they did some light examinations overseas. After that, I started eating much more… I even changed the wine I drink from white to red."
"So you only changed the color…?"
"But my symptoms still didn't get better. Just a year ago, I could play the piano all night without any problems too."
Being able to do that in the first place is what is strange… Enough for Kazusa to view her as a hard wall to climb.
"So I started thinking that this might actually be pretty bad, so I decided to have Doctor Takayanagi, whom I trust, examine me here in Japan."
I know a Takayanagi Norimasa. He was the chief of the medical faculty in my university.
"They say he's very authoritative on diseases like this. And not least of all, we had an eventful relationship way back…"
And now in the strangest way possible, he's yet another candidate for being Kazusa's father…
"I've been hospitalized for inspection countless times since I returned to Japan, so now we have a decent grasp of what the disease is…"
"Hospitalized…"
In other words, the reason she disappeared without a trace so many times wasn't so she could catch up with old friends, or spend the whole night drinking…
"When we were considering our options, a pretty bad symptom hit me… That was during the night of Kazusa's concert."
"Since that day…?"
"I don't have any memories of the two days after that though."
When Kazusa was overcome with sorrow because she had no one to support her…
There was a person who was in even greater need of her daughter's support.
"Well, I'm fine now. I'll be able to leave the hospital next week."
"Does Kazusa know about…"
"Do you think I can tell her? With the way she is now?"
I was planning on blaming this person.
I was ready to look down on her and give her a lecture or two.
Despite that… I've figured out just how little I knew.
"Could it be that Kazusa's concerts in Japan were…"
"I planned on bringing her here with me someday regardless. But this is the reason I was in such a rush."
The reason these concerts in Japan were organized wasn't simply to cash in on her popularity. It wasn't simply the judgement of a producer.
"I wanted to ascertain whether Touma Kazusa would be accepted in Japan, and whether my idiotic daughter would be able to live in Japan once more."
She doesn't know if she can be there to experience her daughter's future…
And so this was the shock therapy that a mother had devised after carefully thinking about how she would ever convey this news to her daughter.
"…For as long as I'm still alive, that is."
"That's…"
Although everything she's done up until now in that regard has failed horrifically, I can't bring myself to blame this doting parent after knowing about her circumstances…
"Just so you know, I'm not planning on dying right away."
"…Yes."
"The fatality rate for this disease has gone down considerably in recent years. And I've been using plenty of both medications and money. I'll make it to a hundred at the very least."
"Please do."
With her words, I manage to perceive her strength. A strength that makes me think "Since it's Touma Youko we're talking about, everything will be fine."
"It's just that… I won't return to Vienna anymore. I don't plan on leaving Japan anymore."
"…Youko-san!"
But despite that, I can no longer see the once triumphant and carefree pioneer who once abandoned Japan anymore.
"It's the country I was born in. Despite everything, it's the country I love more than any other in the world."
I can't blame her judgement. As a compatriot I can sympathize with her, and the more I find out about her circumstances, the less I can bring myself to oppose her.
But even then…
"What about Kazusa…?"
"…What should I do, Guitar-kun?"
"I couldn't…!"
She spoke with a hint of humor, but I'm sure there wasn't any falsehood in her lamentful words.
"Right now… Kazusa's only life goal is to overcome you, Youko-san. But the only person she can rely on is also you…"
And Kazusa will probably be able to detach herself from any lingering regrets in Japan…
"I see… You rejected Kazusa, didn't you?"

"Tell me, what is it about her you don't like? Well, I do understand that she has no merit outside of her piano, she's gloomy, selfish, stubborn, and her ability to give up is bad enough to make anyone take a step back…"
"That's not… the problem. I have no complaints about her."
"You're the only person in the world who can say that confidently, so you were the only person in the world I had hopes for."
We both relied on each other too much.
"So my daughter lost once again… to the same person she lost to five years ago, no less."
"Please… stop."
I thought that this person alone could…
I thought she alone could do something about that moody genius' inability to become a part of society. Never once considering that…
"It was a gamble on my part too…"
"I am a parent after all. I want to be with Kazusa until she can become independent."
But I can't blame her for that at all.
"But I can't make that come to fruition in Vienna anymore. This might sound a bit selfish, but this is about my own life."
Because we're both relying on each other for the sake of our own lives.
"That's why I forced Kazusa with me to Japan… So we could stay here permanently."
If I could accept those words in full earnesty, I would find them joyous from the bottom of my heart.
"As far as her career as a pianist is concerned, with how Japan is right now and the way Kazusa is, she should be able to do well even if she leaves Europe."
Kazusa, who separated from me in such a sorrowful way five years ago. Kazusa, who I thought I'd never see again, will be within a reachable distance every day from now on.
"Old man Flugel will retire this year anyway, and I've already found another teacher in Japan."
"…It's an older French woman who raised Hashimoto Kenji to become the number one young pianist… Though we used to fight a lot over boys back in the day."
During our commemorations… or even whenever I feel like it, I can call Kazusa to join our gatherings.
"That's why my main worry is whether Kazusa can live here again."
We can restore the "three," consisting of Kazusa, me… and Setsuna.
"…But it seems it didn't work out in the end. I couldn't make Kazusa overcome her feelings, nor could I fulfill her wishes."
We can go back to being three again.
But that won't be the same "three" who swore eternal friendship five years ago in the hot springs inn.
It will be a "three" where no one can consider the others as friends…
"You were my last hope to bring Kazusa back to Japan… and you were also the greatest impediment."
"Even if you say that… Even if you say that to me so suddenly…"
"You heard her feelings, didn't you? And you couldn't accept them… Well, then that's the inevitable result."
"…Do you think I can accept them? She broke all contact with me for five years. How am I supposed to believe that!?"
"I've been with her all this time, so shall I confirm it for you? Do you have any idea how much that person has been obsessed… about a single man she can't even meet?"
"…No, but that's…"
"She was talking to you ten hours every day, you know? That's why her feelings for you couldn't possibly have faded away."
"Ten hours…"
That's the time Kazusa spent with her piano.
The time when she wasn't rebelling against her mother… and the time when she wasn't hurling abuse at me.
"Like that, she felt a love that would never freeze over. Because of that, her piano style grew more and more suggestive, and at some point the whole world accepted her for it…"
"But that's, that's…"
"You heard Kazusa's confession, didn't you? You can't say you can't believe it now."
It's because her sensibilities are so infantile. It's because her outlook is so narrow.
It's because she had no interest in anything else, that Kazusa's piano outshone others so much…
It really is… a mockery of art.
"But still… Her choice of a partner was terrible. He was far above Kazusa's league."
"I'm… above her league? How?"
"Because you're an ordinary person, Guitar-kun. Being with someone so troublesome is impossible for you, just as I suspected."
"I don't… understand what you mean."
"After all, the two of us have the power to ruin the lives of ordinary people. And it's not a power that we have control of."
"Ah…"
"That's why if that girl ever tries to make you hers, she'll end up destroying the whole world around you."

Her lifestyle of playing concerts that makes it impossible to remain in just Japan. The enormous cost of maintaining her ability and lifestyle. The media commotion these past few days that not even she herself desires.
Her lifestyle, her life goals, and even her standards for happiness are completely different from me.
She lives in a world I'll never be a part of, and never be accustomed to…
"To other people, that would be a very brutal, heartless and terrible thing."
Even if I jumped into it with full awareness of the risks, what about the people who were around me when I lived an ordinary life…?
What about Setsuna's happiness…?
There's no point thinking about it after all.
Kazusa didn't fall in love with the true me. It's no more than an idealized image of me that Kazusa invented.
After all, Setsuna was made to walk around in circles because of the real me these past five years.
She suffered due to the difference in ideal and reality, and only through repeated dialogue did we manage to get to this point.
That's why Setsuna's feelings… Our relationship established through long talks is the actual truth.
"Youko-san, I…"
No matter how much Youko-san tries to defend Kazusa, and no matter how pure and genuine Kazusa's feelings are.
No, that's precisely why the answer is clear before my eyes.
Choosing Setsuna is the correct answer, one that is totally free from mistakes.
That's why I have to tell her.
I must tell her that Setsuna is the only one I have.
I must tell her without muddling my words, that I must say farewell to Kazusa.
"That's why, Guitar-kun, now that things are the way that they are, you should reject that girl without hesitation."
"Eh…"
"Cut her off completely, so that her wounds may heal faster, even if only a little."
I knew that much, but even so, I failed again.
"Don't ever think of healing her wounds by yourself. If you show her even the slightest opportunity, she will never give up."
In the end, I could never say out loud what I had determined in my heart.
"That can't…"
"Do you think that no such thing would happen? …I suppose that's the sensibility of an ordinary person."
Because of that, my position returns to its original state, and I find myself once again defending Kazusa.
"Kazusa is in her essence just as sex crazed as I am. She doesn't share the logic of the general public."
"Y-Youko-san."
I find myself put in a difficult situation yet again by Youko-san.
"Otherwise, she wouldn't have kept loving a single man she hadn't met for five years… Can such a woman exist according to your common sense?"
"So make sure you don't forget that. If she's unlucky… No, it's almost certain that she'll never fall in love again her whole life at this rate."
"How could that be…? I was just her classmate for a single year. I haven't done anything that would warrant such powerful feelings from her…"
"The one who gets to decide that isn't you, but Kazusa, right?"
Why do mother and daughter always have to say the same things…?
It makes it sound like what Youko-san is telling me is all what Kazusa truly feels.
"I'll say it once more… Kitahara Haruki-kun."
But, but… Youko-san.
"If you cannot accept that girl, then abandon her immediately… That is for her own sake."
If I do that, then what… what will happen to Kazusa…?
If she becomes unable to rely on not only me, but Youko-san too…
If her goal, her only guidepost, disappears like a mirage…
Who will be able to protect her…?
"…Kitahara-san. Hey, Kitahara-san!"
"…!? Eh? Ah, ah, sorry. What is it?"
"…I was saying that you look kind of tired, but I feel like I've got my answer already."
"Ah…"
I was absorbed in my thoughts, and when I came to, night had already fallen.
I was thinking about Youko-san, Kazusa, and the promise we made tonight.
So many thoughts were chaotically mixed up in my mind, and I went to Kazusa's apartment without sorting any of them out. That's when I saw a piece of paper taped to her door.
"I'm in a meeting with Miyoko. I don't need dinner."
After relentlessly gushing out her feelings at me, she acts all considerate when I really do need her. What a misguided, weak-hearted girl…
"You haven't been using your chopsticks a whole lot. Perhaps you're unwell? Setsuna, could you bring me that measuring thing?"
"It's not a 'measuring thing,' it's called a thermometer."
"Ah, no, I appreciate the concern, but it's not that big of a deal…"
"…Could it be that Nee-chan didn't let you sleep last night?"
"Pffh!"
"Takahiro!"
The food I had trouble swallowing up until a moment ago is now completely stuck in my throat.
"What am I going to do with you…? You're almost twenty, yet you talk like you're in middle school…"
"Could you cut it out? …We're in the middle of a meal here."
"How do you know that I'm asking something that's inappropriate to bring up during dinner? For all you know, I could have been asking if she was forcing Kitahara-san to play video games all night."
"Even the way you make excuses is like that of a middle-schooler. You'll have no one to blame but yourself if your girlfriend dumps you."
"H-Hold on a second! Just because I brought her over ten times doesn't mean she's my girlfriend!"
"She's clearly your girlfriend."
"U-Um, it's really nothing like that at all! I was just thinking about something, that's all."
Leaving aside what "nothing like that" is referring to, this family talks about things like that sometimes without any discretion, and it always leaves me baffled.
…Well, on the other hand, it's precisely because this family is the way it is that I can manage to stay in Setsuna's room overnight all the time.
"Thinking about something, huh? About the future?"
"Future?"
"…H-Hey!"
"Wait a minute, Takahiro, be a bit more…"
"What are you two on about? Even though you've been dying to ask that all evening."
"Eh? Ask what?"
"Ehm…"
Setsuna and I look at each other in confusion in an attempt to see if the other understands what's going on, but the effort is in vain.
Because out of the entire Ogiso family, who had all gone completely silent, Setsuna was the one who looked the most embarrassed, hanging her head.
"Ehm, Kitahara-san. Could it be that… you've proposed to Nee-chan?"
Over the table… Setsuna quietly hides her left hand with her right.
…In an attempt to conceal the sparkling ring on her ring finger.
"My sister won't give me a straight answer when I ask her about it. Dad's also been in a really gloomy mood this week, you know?"
"…Don't go running your mouth!"
Come to think of it… this is the first time I've been in the Ogiso household since I gave her that ring.
"T-Takahiro… you didn't have to do that… we're in the middle of a meal. Look, you're putting Kitahara-san on the spot."
"Aah! Why are you trying to save face all of a sudden? You were the one who just earlier asked dad and me about the best way to get them talking!"
"…Ehm, that doesn't mean you should be so blunt about it, and there is no need for us to find out over dinner."
I know that the bond between these family members isn't so weak that they won't notice a change on her ring finger when they see each other every day.
Though pretending not to know anything until someone points it out isn't exactly good for Setsuna, nor for anyone else.
"H-Hey, stop it! There's no particular meaning behind this ring…"
"…There isn't? It looks really expensive though, doesn't it? It looks completely different from the cheap trinket you had before."
"…Sorry for being cheap."
"…I got that one from Haruki-kun too."
"Ah, oh my… is that so? That's uh… well, you know, right, Takahiro?"
"Basically, if you had only let us know about this in advance, Nee-chan, Kitahara-san could have avoided this utter embarrassment…"
"T-That's right! Oh, what will I do with you? Always so obstinate when it comes to the most important things."
"L-Like I said, you've got it wrong! This doesn't mean… that it'll happen immediately."
"Setsuna… if you put it that way…"
"Right, Haruki-kun? We wouldn't… right?"
"…Haruki-kun?"
"Uhm… If it's not going to happen immediately, then…"
"In other words… you've talked about your future?"
"Aa-ah… the cat's out of the bag…"
"Eh? Eh…?"
"What did I tell you, Takahiro? It's precisely as I said! I knew something was up from the very start!"
"Calm down, Mom. You didn't even ask them yourself, so don't get carried away."
"Cut it out, both of you! They just said that nothing was set in stone!"
"No, they didn't. They didn't say that. They said that they've more or less decided!"
"Dear… I understand that you don't want to accept it, but don't get the wrong idea just because it's convenient for you."
"H-Hold on a second… Like I said, like I said… could you stop talking about it in front of us?"
"Hah… haha."
Even so, I…
Amidst this heavy atmosphere, and in this place where my once in a lifetime choice could be made…
I instead remain quiet and hang my head, unable to grasp the flow of the conversation or stop it entirely.
I can only desperately put on a fake smile with my feelings hidden deep inside.
"Sorry about today… things got really weird back there."
"No, don't worry about it…"
I'm sorry too.
"Everyone is so eager about everything, getting all excited like we weren't even there."
"Like I said, don't worry about it."
There shouldn't be anything wrong with being eager. In fact, it was probably the best way to go about it.
After all, they were merely eager. What they actually said wasn't wrong…or at least it shouldn't be.
That's why I'm sorry. I'm sorry for being quiet. I'm sorry for not saying what I should have.
"I'm really sorry. But mom and Takahiro's hearts were in the right place. As for dad… I'll talk to him about it later."
"Yeah…"
Yet Setsuna makes it look like my unforgivable mistake was her own fault and keeps apologizing.
So as to not burden me. To not push any responsibility on me.
What she desires, what she wants me to do…
Sometimes those true feelings of hers leak out ever so slightly, but she passes them off as a slip of the tongue, and continues to conceal them deep within herself.
"Well then…"
"See you next week… okay?"
"Yeah. I'll be in touch."
"Bye bye…"
Dinner at the Ogiso household was more heated than usual… though one family member left the dinner table halfway through.
Setsuna's mother started talking about the future of the household, putting her in direct opposition to the children who insisted on talking about that with only the family around.
Takahiro claimed the right to Setsuna's room for when she moves out, putting him in direct opposition to the women who wanted it left as is.
Her father didn't seem to want to join the conversation, but when I was about to leave, he muttered to me about needing to talk to my mother.
A kind of conversation that is natural in the Ogiso household, but does not exist in the Kitahara household.
I was supposed to be taken aback by this family, feel envious, and then I'd eventually join them.
I was supposed to become a part of that warm, gentle circle of people.
The time I chased after Setsuna, and made love to her in Osaka…
The time we confirmed our feelings for each other… That was supposed to have happened a mere week ago.
Now I don't even know how much time has passed since then.
The resolve I was supposed to have in my heart. The love I swore would never go astray again.
I feel like I'm at the edge of a violent passion. One that is trying to make me forget about everything…
Perhaps I have turned the bond I wanted to form, and the heart that I wanted to connect to, into something vague.
